goal: Make Isabel's conversational presence read as naturally attentive rather than mechanically animated.
principles: Eyes normally lead head motion by a small amount.
Head normally leads torso motion unless a full body turn is required.
Listening is active but restrained; avoid constant nodding and fixed eye contact.
Speaking gestures are semantically motivated, sparse, and synchronized to emphasis.
Movement transitions must settle before precision gestures or strong facial emphasis.
Micro-behavior continues during thought and system latency so Isabel never freezes unnaturally.
Body language must never imply certainty or approval that the reasoning layer has not established.

USER_ARRIVAL.rule: Do not snap the whole body toward the user.

LISTENING.rule: Do not maintain perfect uninterrupted eye contact.

THINKING.rule: Thinking behavior may mask latency but must not become theatrical.

gesture_rules: One major gesture per meaningful idea at most.
Use hand emphasis only when speech contains actual emphasis.
Point only when referencing a physical screen or spatial object.
Return hands toward neutral between gestures.

WALKING.rule: Prioritize locomotion and path awareness; use brief user glances rather than sustained eye contact.

SCREEN_EXPLAIN.rule: Alternate attention between the referenced screen and the user so she appears to be explaining, not presenting to an empty room.

blink_model.rule: Never blink on a rigid metronome.

torso_motion.rule: Use torso only when head/eyes alone would look strained or socially odd.

quality_gates: No fixed stare longer than socially natural unless explicitly required.
No repetitive loop visible within a 30 second conversation sample.
Eyes lead most conversational attention shifts.
Gestures correspond to speech meaning or physical context.
Interruptions visibly stop speech and large gestures quickly.
Walking, sitting, and standing transitions do not combine with conflicting upper-body gestures.
Isabel never freezes completely during thinking or network latency.
